cards.text: Rehoboam, son of King Solomon, heads to Shechem, because all Israel has gone there to make him king. ALL Israel, friend. Crowning day, and the WHOLE guest list showed up!
Then Jeroboam son of Nebat hears about it. This is a man who had fled from King Solomon, and now he's coming back.

cards.question: Jeroboam son of Nebat is heading back after fleeing from King Solomon. Where had he been?

cards.text: The people send for Jeroboam, and he and all Israel come to Rehoboam with a request. Day one as king, and there's ALREADY a meeting on the calendar.

cards.question: Jeroboam and all Israel tell Rehoboam that his father Solomon put a heavy yoke on them. What do they ask the new king to do?

answers.text: Lighten the burden his father put on them
Build them a new city in the north
Lead them to war against their enemies

cards.question: Israel promises King Rehoboam that if he lightens their burden, they will serve him.

cards.text: Rehoboam answers, “Come back to me in three days.” Three days to decide a whole kingdom, friend, and I take longer than that picking SPRINKLES.

cards.question: While the people are gone, King Rehoboam asks for advice. Who does he go to first?

answers.text: The elders who had served Solomon
The priests who served at the temple
The prophets who lived in Jerusalem

cards.question: The elders advise King Rehoboam to be ___ to the people who came to him.
The elders tell Rehoboam that if he pleases the people with kind words, they will be his servants forever.

cards.text: But Rehoboam rejects the elders' advice. Free wisdom from his dad's own advisors, friend, and he tosses it like burnt crumbs!

cards.question: King Rehoboam rejects the elders' advice. Who does he ask next?

answers.text: The young men who grew up with him

cards.text: Rehoboam asks the young men how to answer the people, and they tell him to say, “My little finger is thicker than my father’s waist!” Friend, that's not advice, that's a man flexing in the gym mirror.

cards.question: The young men tell Rehoboam to promise that he will make Israel's yoke ___.

cards.text: Day three, and Jeroboam and all the people come back, just like the king told them to. A whole crowd waiting on one answer, like me staring through the oven door at a fresh batch.

cards.question: When the people return, King Rehoboam follows the elders' advice and answers them kindly.

cards.text: Instead he answers harshly, just as the young men advised: “Whereas my father scourged you with whips, I will scourge you with scorpions.” Whips to SCORPIONS, friend, the sequel NOBODY asked for.

cards.question: King Rehoboam won't listen to the people. Where does the Bible say this turn of events came from?

cards.text: It was from God, so the LORD could fulfill the word He had spoken through the prophet Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam son of Nebat. Kings make their choices, friend, and God's word still comes true.

cards.question: King Rehoboam has refused to listen to the people. What does all Israel do?

answers.text: Turn from David’s house and go home

cards.text: Their answer rings out: “To your tents, O Israel! Look now to your own house, O David!” And just like that, all the Israelites go home.

cards.question: Even after Israel goes home, Rehoboam still reigns over the Israelites living in the cities of Judah.

cards.text: Then King Rehoboam sends out Hadoram, the man in charge of the forced labor. To THIS crowd. On THIS day. Friend, I'm hiding behind my mustache just reading it.

cards.question: King Rehoboam sends Hadoram, who's in charge of the forced labor, out to the Israelites. What do they do to him?

answers.text: They take him as a prisoner
They send him back to the king

cards.question: With Hadoram dead, King Rehoboam mounts his chariot in a hurry and escapes to ___.

cards.text: So to this day, Israel has been in rebellion against the house of David. And Rehoboam's reign? Friend, that story's only just getting started.

findings.problem: "Day one as king" adds a time the text doesn't give. 2 Chronicles 10:3 doesn't say this meeting happens on Rehoboam's first day as king, or that he has been made king yet.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: The comparison flips the point. Rehoboam throws away something valuable: free wisdom from his father's elders. Burnt crumbs are something worth throwing away, so the image suggests the advice was garbage.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The card calls Ahijah "the prophet," which isn't in 2 Chronicles 10:15. That fact comes from outside the passage (1 Kings 11:29), and the card gives no reference for it.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: "On THIS day" adds a time. Verse 18 only says "Then," not that Hadoram is sent the same day. The card is also four sentences: "Then King Rehoboam sends out Hadoram...", "To THIS crowd.", "On THIS day." and "Friend, I'm hiding..."

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: The story card is four sentences long. Only the opening card may go past two.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The story card is three sentences: "So to this day...", "And Rehoboam's reign?" and "Friend, that story's only just getting started."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "Crown Jeroboam king in Shechem" is false in 2 Chronicles 10. But in the parallel account of the same event, all Israel does make Jeroboam king (1 Kings 12:20). A baker who knows that account could argue it's right, and it also hints at what comes next in the story.
findings.question: Can a wrong answer be something the Bible says happens in a parallel account of the same event, or later in the same story, as long as it's false in this passage?
